newsitem.title: UK: Britain foils possible IRA mass breakout.
newsitem.headline: Britain foils possible IRA mass breakout.

text.p: Britain has foiled a possible mass breakout by Irish Republican Army (IRA) prisoners after discovering a tunnel in Northern Ireland's maximum security Maze prison.
The tunnel, apparently equipped with electric lighting, was discovered late on Sunday. It led from a block which houses 95 of the jail's 297 republican convicts.

"At no stage did any prisoners escape and all have been accounted for," a British spokesman said as officials probed the security breach at the jail which houses one of the largest concentrations of guerrilla prisoners in western Europe.
The inmates are segregated into blocks housing republican IRA activists and Protestant guerrillas.
Pro-British Protestant leaders demanded an immediate clampdown on convicted IRA guerrillas.
"Serious sentences have got to be passed on those responsible for this escape attempt," Ulster Unionist Party security spokesman Ken Maginnis told BBC radio.
Peter Robinson, deputy leader of the Democratic Unionist Party, said guerrillas had been given too much freedom in their cell blocks and allowed to dictate to warders on the timing of searches.
"They (warders) need to ask the permission of the so-called commander of the wing before they enter the wing, that's the extent of the control the IRA inmates have," Robinson said.
"Prison officers do not believe the prison establishment will back them up. There needs to be a complete review of security," he told the BBC.
The Maze prison was the scene in 1983 of the largest prison breakout in British history when 38 republican inmates escaped. Some are still at large.
British officials said the tunnel did not extend to outer walls of the Maze which is near a busy motorway.
"A tunnel was discovered by a routine patrol...A full and thorough investigation is now taking place," a spokesman for the Northern Ireland prison service said.

The IRA's political wing Sinn Fein was excluded from all-party peace talks on Northern Ireland which started in June last year and which were suspended earlier this month ahead of a British general election on May 1.
